attack_indicators: presence of suspicious URLs often unrelated to sender domain
use of urgent or lucrative offers in subject lines (e.g., 'Part-Time opportunity - $2000/week')
inclusion of financial or personal gain narratives (e.g., inheritance scams, fake job offers)
presence of misspellings, grammatical errors, and unusual formatting
inclusion of contact information with free email providers or suspicious domains
references to well-known brands or institutions to build trust (e.g., Barclays Bank, Canadian Pharmacy)
use of obfuscated or non-standard URLs with uncommon TLDs or domain names
inclusion of pharmaceutical product promotions with direct links
use of social engineering tactics appealing to emotions or urgency
attack_signatures: signature pattern 1: Emails containing financial scams referencing large abandoned sums with detailed backstories and requests for cooperation (e.g., 'I am Mr. Tim Kennedy, senior credit officer... abandoned sum of 12.5 million British pounds')
signature pattern 2: Phishing emails promoting online pharmacies with direct URLs and claims of FDA approval or discounts (e.g., 'fast loading us based online pharmacy http://www.nmedbuy.org/')
signature pattern 3: Use of short, spam-like bodies with lists of cheap medications and embedded suspicious URLs (e.g., 'Viagra >>>> High Quality... http://adhviw.summerballs.info/?38872604')
technical_markers: measurable marker 1: URLs with uncommon or newly registered domains, often with numeric or random character strings (e.g., 'http://asterduskyhah.com/')
measurable marker 2: Subject lines containing monetary amounts or urgent calls to action (e.g., '$2000/week', 'Online Drugstore Announce Discounts')
measurable marker 3: Email bodies exceeding 500 words with narrative scams or social engineering content, often including personal names and contact details
normal_indicators: benign emails with professional or neutral subject lines related to business, academic, or news content
email bodies containing structured, coherent, and topic-consistent text without suspicious links
absence of unsolicited financial offers or urgent calls to action
presence of legitimate organizational signatures and contact information consistent with sender domain
use of standard language and formatting with minimal spelling or grammatical errors
baseline_metrics: average email body length typically between 100 to 1000 words depending on context
URLs, if present, correspond to known or reputable domains matching sender source
subject lines generally descriptive without monetary or urgent inducements
low frequency of suspicious or obfuscated URLs (<5% of benign emails)
absence of repeated suspicious keywords such as 'discount', 'free', 'urgent', or monetary amounts
